name: IsoScene
description: Place kind table with table:{name,columns,rows,indexed?,locked?,duplicateKey?} next to a database to show the actual records. Timed steps support timer, count, meter, progress, ttl, retry, queue, think, react, say and mood. A reply step such as cache→app returns on an existing request link. Links can clean or drop packets and carry keys or coins. Use badge on objects or timed steps for animated lookup, worker, access or health states. Use none to clear, or {icon,text,tone} for a custom Lucide badge. Media badges cover broadcast, editorial review, verification, attribution, embargo and signal loss. Change embargo to released in a timed step to open the lock. Media steps can animate reach, engage, compare (saw it vs understood it), rating, revenue, trust, cycle, sentiment and survey. Sentiment is [positive,neutral,negative] and must total 100. Media links support flow:"wave", via:"leader", noise:true and dashed feedback. Timed spread uses outgoing links up to depth; gate uses a link into and out of the editor. Use frame:[before,after], agenda ordered by coverage priority, bubble, race with rumour and correction speeds, attention, opinion:{from,to}, split:[a,b], or headline updates. Target people for crowd changes. Show both sides of race and compare together, distinguish attention or sharing from belief, and identify illustrative statistics as example numbers in narration. Use links[].bidirectional=true for two-way traffic. Label the outbound arrow with label and the reverse arrow with returnLabel. Set replyAfter (e.g. 0.5) to play them in sequence. Isometric "paper" diagram: 3D-looking servers, databases, caches, clouds, people, medical objects (hospital, doctor, patient bed, ambulance, pill bottle, syringe, heart monitor, microscope, test tubes, DNA), school objects (school, teacher with whiteboard, student desk, bookshelf, graduation cap, backpack, globe on a stand, certificate, pencil and notebook), finance objects (bank, coin stack, wallet, credit card, ATM, safe, piggy bank, cash bundle, stock chart board, calculator, receipt), retail and business objects (shop, shopping cart, delivery parcel on a conveyor, cash register, warehouse, price tag, shopping bag, factory, office desk, handshake, meeting table) and transport objects (car, truck, road, bus, train, airplane, ship, bicycle, traffic light, fuel pump, map pin), all plus everyday objects (house, tree, clock, animated bar and pie charts, chat bubble, sun, weather, trophy, flag, lightbulb, gear, magnifier, warning, checkmark, cross) and role figures (chef, worker, police). AI and emerging media objects include an AI-generated-content label, synthetic voice, altered-image comparison, recommendation Politics and public affairs: parliament, ballotbox, campaignrally, publicmeeting, protestplacard, governmentoffice. Public relations: pressrelease, podium, pressconference, spokesperson, mediakit, crisiscentre. TV and film: studiocamera, teleprompter, studiolights, controlmonitors, obvan, clapperboard, cinemaprojector, cinemascreen, filmreel, storyboard, editingtimeline, theatrestage. Digital: socialpost, scrollingfeed, videoplayer, livestream, comments, repost, notification, hashtag. Advertising: productdisplay, campaignboard, sponsoredpost, adplacement, paywall, adpayment. system and verified-content panel. Radio, audio and podcast objects include headphones, a mixing console, a boom microphone, a studio speaker, a field recorder and a podcast booth. Clocks and gears turn, charts grow, ECG traces pulse, ambulance lights flash, and links support car flow. All objects are dropping in and animating on a paper grid. Communication fundamentals include envelope, sender, receiver, encoder, decoder, feedback loop and noise interference. Steps (timed as a fraction of the narration) change loads (⚙ 59% pills), highlight, add notes and move the camera. Use for systems, architecture, flows, networking, scaling, how-things-work, healthcare, education, finance, retail, logistics, journalism, newsrooms, AI, synthetic media, misinformation and media literacy. With no objects it is a paper title card (title, subtitle, points).

name: ScreenScene
description: A website or app being used, in the paper style: a laptop, monitor, phone or browser window shows pages built from blocks (nav, hero, heading, text, image, cards, card, button, input, list, banner, footer); a timed script moves the mouse, clicks, types into inputs (or password dots), scrolls, opens other pages (address bar + loading bar), shows toasts and zooms in on an element. Use to show what the user does and sees (sign up, search, buy, log in, submit a form). Add "diagram" (IsoScene props: objects, links, steps) to show the screen on the left and what happens behind it on the right at the same time (the click on the left, the request travelling on the right).

name: PhoneScene

Screens are built from blocks (header, heading, text, image, amount, input, button, list, cards, chat, banner, tabs). The title and each action's note appear as steps beside the phone. Use for mobile apps, phone logins and OTP, payments, push notifications, messaging.

name: PacketScene
description: A packet's journey, in the paper style: devices left to right (branches show other paths), an envelope travels between them, opens to show its fields (IP, port, TTL, headers), a router reads one field and picks a path (that link lights up), fields change on the way (TTL, NAT), a packet can be dropped. Steps: send / route (to), open, close, read (field), change (field, value), note (text), drop. Use for networking, HTTP, TCP/IP, DNS, routing, NAT, firewalls.

name: ArrayScene
description: An array as bars or boxes (paper style). Give "values" (up to 12) and "algorithm": bubble | selection | insertion | merge | quick | binary-search | linear-search (+ "target") and every comparison and swap is traced automatically with i/j pointers, comparison/swap counters and the pseudocode line lighting up. Or give your own "steps": compare {i,j}, swap {i,j}, set {i,value}, sorted {i}, pointer {name,i}, range {lo,hi}, found {i}, note; every step may have a "note".

name: StackScene
description: A stack (LIFO bucket, open at the top) or a queue (FIFO lane: in at the back, out at the front) in the paper style. "kind": stack | queue, "items" already inside, "steps": push {value} | pop | peek | note (enqueue/dequeue work too). Popped items line up in an "out" row so the order is visible. Use for undo history, call stack, print queue, BFS queue.

name: HashScene
description: A hash table in the paper style: a key goes through the hash function (the sum is shown), "% size" picks a bucket, and the key flies there; keys landing in the same bucket grow a chain (collision). get / delete walk the chain node by node. Give "size" (buckets, 3-12), optional "entries", and "steps": insert {key, value} | get {key} | delete {key} | note. Buckets are computed (sum of letter codes, or the number) unless a step gives "bucket". "act" and "cat" collide.

name: TreeScene
description: A tree in the paper style. kind "bst": insert walks down comparing (7 > 5 → right) and the node pops in; "avl": after insert/delete the tree rebalances and nodes glide through each rotation; "tree": any hierarchy given as "tree": {label, children:[...]} (file system, DOM, org chart). "values" are inserted at the start; "steps": insert {value, parent for "tree"} | delete {value} | find {value} | traverse {order: inorder|preorder|postorder|bfs} | visit {value} | note.

name: GraphScene
description: A graph in the paper style: "nodes" (strings are fine; optional x/y), "edges" ([from, to, weight?] or "A-B"), "directed". "steps": bfs {from} spreads level by level with the queue shown; dfs {from} goes deep and backtracks with the stack shown; dijkstra {from, to} settles the nearest node, relaxes edges (distances on nodes) and lights the shortest path; path {nodes:[...]}, visit {value}, edge {from,to}, note. Use for maps/routes, social networks, dependencies, web crawling.

name: LinkedListScene
description: A singly linked list in the paper style: [value | next] boxes, arrows, a "head" tag and null at the end. "values" (up to 7), "steps": insert {value, index | after: value} (new node appears, its next points at the successor, then the previous arrow swings to it), append, prepend, delete {value | index} (the arrow swings past the node, it drops out), find {value} (a curr pointer walks), reverse (arrows flip one by one), note. Shows why insert is O(1) once you are there and find is O(n).

name: EventLoopScene
description: How JavaScript / Node.js runs code (paper style): code with the running line, the CALL STACK (frames with local vars), the HEAP (objects; a var with value "@id" draws an arrow to it), Node/Web APIs (timers, I/O), the MICROTASK queue (promises), the TASK queue, the event loop and the console. Only used panels are drawn. "steps": call {name, vars} | return | log {text} | api {name, callback, id} | done {id} (API finished → task queue) | queue {name, to: micro|task} | tick (event loop moves the next microtask, else task, onto the stack) | alloc {id, label, fields, var} | set {name, value} | free {id} | note; each may have "line". Presets without steps: "event-loop" (A D C B) and "memory" (stack vs heap, GC).

name: PlotScene
description: A live function graph (paper style): curves from formulas like "a*x^2 + b", "sin(k*x)", "m*x + c" are recalculated every frame, so "set" steps morph the curve while sliders and numbers count to the new value. Steps: set {a: 3} | trace {x} (dot moves along the curve, y calculated) | mark {x} (pinned point with its value) | tangent {x} (slope) | area {from, to} (integral) | zoom {x: [min,max], y} | clear | note. Give "curves" (1-3, use * ^ and brackets), "params" (starting values), "x" range. y range fits automatically. For data that changes, use LiveChartScene.

b moves the whole curve down

shaded area = the integral from -1 to 2

name: LiveChartScene
description: A bar / line / race chart (paper style) whose numbers change on screen. Values come from "series" data or a "formula" over a range ("P*(1+r)^t", var t, from 0 to 10, params {P, r}). Steps: set {r: 0.1} (every value recalculated, bars grow) | set {label, value} | set {values: [...]} | add {label?, by} | scale {by} | append {label, value} | remove {label} | sort {order} | highlight {label} | reveal {count} (bars or the line appear one by one) | note. Numbers count while they move, the axis rescales, race bars swap rank. The panel shows the formula, params and the worked calculation; "stats": total, average, max, min, last, change.

steps.note: Each year the balance grows by r
Double the rate to 10%: every year is recalculated
After 10 years: more than double the start

name: MediaTheoryScene
description: Four isometric media theory animations: communication sends text through noise and returns feedback (a feedback extension to Shannon–Weaver); agenda grows a headline across days and audience attention; two-step flow fans media out through opinion leaders; gratifications lets people choose news, entertainment or social media. Illustrative teaching examples.

name: RaceScene
description: Two simultaneous split-screen lanes with moving progress bars and stopwatches. Supply exactly two lanes {label, seconds, color?}; lower seconds wins and receives a checkmark. Equal times show a tie. Both start together, finish according to their relative durations, and hold results before the scene ends. Useful for cache versus no cache, algorithms, or before/after speed comparisons.

title.default: The same request. A faster finish.

example.title: The same request. A faster finish.

name: LiveDashboardScene
description: Animated monitoring dashboard with continuously moving latency and throughput graphs, live KPI values and server status. The server fails at failureAt and recovers at recoveryAt (fractions of scene duration); latency rises and falls while throughput drops and returns. Customize server, baselineMs, peakMs and requestsPerSecond. Illustrative simulated metrics, not a live data connection.

title.default: A failure you can see in the numbers

example.title: A failure you can see in the numbers

name: MapTrackingScene
description: A delivery dot travels along a street-map route, leaving a colored trail as the arrival countdown decreases to zero. Shows origin, destination, courier, progress and delivered confirmation. route is 2–20 normalized [x,y] points (0..1); movement follows segment distance at constant speed. etaSeconds is the illustrative trip time compressed to fit the scene. Schematic map, no external map assets required.

title.default: Follow the delivery, all the way home

example.title: Follow the delivery, all the way home

name: TableScene
description: Animate INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on sample data. Row indices start at zero and refer to the current rows.

name: JoinScene
description: Compute INNER, LEFT or RIGHT equality joins. Connect matching key values and progressively assemble the result, preserving unmatched rows on the selected side. NULL keys do not match.

name: SchemaScene
description: Entity relationship diagram with named table cards, field types, PK and FK labels, and animated relationships connecting specific fields.

name: TransactionScene
description: BEGIN a transaction, animate row changes and COMMIT or ROLLBACK to the original rows. Row indices start at zero and refer to the current rows.

name: RecursionScene
description: Animate factorial(n) calls pushing stack frames, then return values unwinding from factorial(0) = 1.

name: BigORaceScene
description: Compare representative work functions 1, ceil(log2 n), n, n ceil(log2 n), and n² on the same linear scale as n grows.

name: CodeTraceScene
description: Step through supplied code and after-line variable snapshots. Give 1-based line numbers and the complete variables for each step.

name: TruthTableScene
description: Compute and reveal all Boolean input combinations for the chosen unary or binary operator.

name: DPTableScene
description: Fill a grid row by row with the number of right/down paths from the top left. Each new count uses the upper and left neighbors.

name: GeometryScene
description: Draw a right triangle to scale and derive its area and hypotenuse from base and height.

name: NumberLineScene
description: Move a point from one integer to another on a labeled number line and calculate signed displacement.

name: UnitCircleScene
description: Rotate from zero to the supplied angle and display the moving point’s cosine and sine coordinates.

name: VectorScene
description: Draw vector a, add b at its tip, then draw their resultant on equally scaled axes.

name: MatrixMultiplyScene
description: Multiply two conforming matrices up to 3 × 3. Highlight the source row and column and fill each resulting cell.

name: ProbabilityScene
description: Reveal favourable outcomes in a finite equiprobable sample space and calculate their probability.

name: FractionScene
description: Partition one whole into equal pieces, then shade the requested numerator.

name: AlgebraStepsScene
description: Solve ax + b = c by applying inverse operations to both sides. Show the exact ratio and its decimal approximation.

name: BubbleSortScene
description: Visualizes bubble sort as numbered vertical bars, highlighting each comparison and animating adjacent swaps. Use it to introduce passes, comparisons, and the final sorted result.
